texts: On day 440 of Year 2, Tessa Brae found a large sky-cat feather near the third cliff-spire.
Tessa Brae added the feather to the feather store.
Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the feather might belong to a new sky-cat.

sentences: On day 440 of Year 2, Tessa Brae found a large sky-cat feather near the third cliff-spire.
Tessa Brae added the feather to the feather store.
Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the feather might belong to a new sky-cat.
parse: (: s4_report_theme (Theme sk_report_1 (And (Member sk_belong_1 belong) (Theme sk_belong_1 sk_feather_1) (Holder sk_belong_1 sk_skycat_1) (Member sk_skycat_1 sky_cat) (Member sk_skycat_1 new) (Might sk_belong_1))) (STV 1.0 0.99))
(: s5_no_action (And (Member sk_take_1 take) (Agent sk_take_1 sk_council_1) (Theme sk_take_1 action) (Past sk_take_1)) (STV 0.0 0.99))

q1_issues.issue: Inside the sealed complement, "the feather might belong to a new sky-cat" gives the prepositional object the role Holder, which the instruction set reserves for the SUBJECT of a possession state (own/have/lack only), and gives the surface subject Theme; the prepositional-verb rule routes such an object to the preposition-named oblique, and a stative intransitive subject to Experiencer.

"near the third cliff-spire" is stored as Location on the finding event, which places the event at the spire rather than near it; Location is glossed "in/at/on" and the surface-preposition doctrine elsewhere forbids folding a proximity preposition into a location/containment head.
(Ordinal sk_cliff_spire_1 3 cliff_spire) fills the <scale> slot with the entity's own class, which is neither the associated ordering event nor an explicit "-est" dimension.

The compound kind sky_cat, used as a class in the sealed complement, gets no genus atom projected to top level, unlike every other compound in the parse (sky_cat_feather, cliff_spire, feather_store) — defensible only if IS-A suppression was intended for the fictional creature.

q2_gaps: A converse possession verb ("X belongs to Y", possessed as subject): Holder/Theme are defined only for possessor-subject verbs (own/have/lack), and the prepositional-verb oblique the rules otherwise mandate gives no route to the Possession form that possession questions are required to query.
An enumerative ordinal ("the third cliff-spire") has no licensed filler for Ordinal's <scale> slot: no associated ordering event, no "-est" dimension, and `unspecified` is Measure-family-only.
An in-world calendar date "day 440 of Year 2" is a day-of-year count, not a day-of-month, and the Time term inventory cannot mark the difference.

"took no action": the QuantifierPhrase companion is mandatory for the explicit quantifier "no", but its shape (QuantifierPhrase <subject> <predicate> "word") has no slot for a "no" sitting on a direct object.
review.notes: The sealing is otherwise handled correctly: a non-factive report with an Experiencer holder, no top-level predication of P, and the seal-internal indefinite sky-cat witness kept inside. Also correct: the past-wrapped copular plus its surface-form Degree level, the fuse-vs-split calls on "large" and "new" against sky_cat_feather, the Goal for "to the feather store", and the strength-0 bundle for the final sentence.

issues.reason: Holder is defined as the subject of a possession / relational state and only for own / have / lack, so filling it with the PP object of "belong to" violates that definition outright, and this is not uncovered territory: the prepositional-verb rule ("referred to the memo" → (To …), never a direct-object role) plus the stative-intransitive-subject rule ("nothing changes and nothing moves" → Experiencer) already license a complete alternative.

"Near" is neither containment nor in / at / on, and the prompt states the entity-side surface-preposition licence is "the same open licence as the event-side preposition-named oblique — never a coined synonym head, always the word actually used", so (Location sk_find_1 sk_cliff_spire_1) asserts the finding happened at the spire when the text says only that it happened nearby.

The gap half stands — Ordinal's <scale> is the associated ordering event or an explicit "-est" dimension and "the third cliff-spire" supplies neither — but the defect half does not, since (Ordinal sk_cliff_spire_1 3 cliff_spire) states nothing false (it is the third among cliff-spires), uses a licensed head, and Core patterns forbids silently dropping the stated restrictive "third".

A fused compound kind's head genus is "always emitted either way" and the seal-projection table routes a sealed P's compound-decomposition atoms to top level as its second item, while the IS-A suppression bar is explicitly the idiom bar's little sibling for lexicalized compounds ("hot dog"), which a transparent novel coinage cannot be — so (Inheritance sky_cat cat) is a determined, missing atom, leaving the minted sky_cat symbol unreachable in the KB.

gaps_confirmed: Converse possession verb ("X belongs to Y", possessed as subject): Holder / Theme are defined only for possessor-subject verbs (own / have / lack), and the preposition-named oblique the rules otherwise mandate feeds no seeded derivation to the (Possession <possessed> <possessor>) form the prompt requires every possession question to query.
Enumerative ordinal ("the third cliff-spire"): Ordinal's <scale> slot has no licensed filler — no associated ordering event, no "-est" dimension, and `unspecified` is Measure-family-only.
In-world calendar date ("day 440 of Year 2"): a day-of-year count, not a day-of-month, and the Time term inventory cannot mark the difference.

"Took no action": the QuantifierPhrase companion is mandatory for every explicit quantifier word the claim consumes, but its (QuantifierPhrase <subject> <predicate> "<word>") shape has no slot for a "no" sitting on a direct object, and here no rule quantifies a range for it to restate — rightly filed as a gap rather than an issue, since an ill-shaped companion would be worse than none.
new_gaps: A novel compound kind naming an invented creature (sky_cat) gives the IS-A suppression test nothing to decide on: the bar the instruction set states is lexicalization ("a hot dog is not a dog"), which a coinage cannot exhibit, so the genus is emitted by default even where the fiction may not support it (a feathered cat) — a licensed form would need a way to mark a genus as surface-derived rather than world-verified, or a stated default for invented kinds.
adjudication.defect_summary: For the belong-to roles the compliant sealed form is (Member sk_belong_1 belong) (Experiencer sk_belong_1 sk_feather_1) (To sk_belong_1 sk_skycat_1) (Might sk_belong_1), which is licensed but loses the possession relation the sentence turns on — the cost recorded in the first confirmed gap. For "near the third cliff-spire" the compliant form is the surface-preposition oblique (Near sk_find_1 sk_cliff_spire_1) in place of Location. For the compound kind, (Inheritance sky_cat cat) belongs at top level beside the seal, per the seal-projection table's second item.
adjudication.notes: The seal itself is handled well: non-factive report with an Experiencer holder, Recipient for the addressee, no top-level predication of P, and the indefinite sky-cat witness correctly kept inside. One cosmetic slip the reviewer did not raise: the witness stem sk_skycat_1 does not match its minted class symbol sky_cat, which the prompt says the symbol is minted from.
